data.narrative:
Exowatt is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Hannan Happi and Jack Abraham, having raised $90M to date. The valuation universe for Climate & Energy includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, though same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the sector proved insufficient in number to support a statistically reliable peer-median analysis.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised of $90M as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression to the next stage yields an implied valuation of $180M. This method accounts for Exowatt's trajectory within the sector's funding patterns but relies on the assumption that a standard Series A multiplier reflects this company's specific risk-return profile.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $153M to $207M, with a median of $180M. Given the single-method basis for this range, key uncertainties center on (1) whether a 2.0x multiplier appropriately captures Exowatt's stage dynamics relative to its specific peer set, and (2) the limited applicability of broader Climate & Energy comparables to this frontier-technology subset. A wider peer-comparable dataset at the same stage would materially strengthen confidence in this range.
